skill_drafts.name: Observation Convention Extension for Custom Metrics
skill_drafts.description: Extend DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention to add custom KeyValue pairs to server request observations while preserving default values. Use when migrating from deprecated TagProvider/TagContributor patterns to the new Observation API in Spring Boot 3.0.
applicable_signals: Deprecated TagProvider or TagContributor classes in codebase
Custom metrics required beyond default observation tags
contraindications: Fully replacing observation convention (implement ServerRequestObservationConvention directly instead)
Adding high-cardinality tags that risk metric cardinality explosion
Overriding metric or trace names (use full convention implementation)
Removing or filtering default observation tags
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Create a new class extending DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention', 'detail': 'public class ExtendedServerRequestObservationConvention extends DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Define protected custom() method', 'detail': 'Extract context data and return KeyValue.of("custom.key", value)'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Register custom convention bean', 'detail': 'Ensure Spring Boot detects and applies the custom convention to RestTemplateBuilder or server request handling'}
triggers: Migrating Spring Boot 2.x TagContributor implementations to Spring Boot 3.0
Migrating Spring Boot 2.x TagProvider implementations to Spring Boot 3.0
Need to inject custom KeyValue pairs into low-cardinality observation context
Extending server request observation with application-specific metric dimensions
constraints: Must extend DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention, not implement from scratch
Custom KeyValue must be extracted from ServerRequestObservationContext
Use .and() to chain custom KeyValue to default KeyValues
cautions: High-cardinality custom tags can cause metric explosion; validate tag values are bounded
Ensure custom KeyValue key names do not conflict with default observation keys
Test that metric and trace names are generated correctly with extended tags
output_contract: Custom KeyValue successfully appended to observation context; metric name and trace name generated correctly with extended tags; default observation tags preserved and not overridden.

examples.input: Spring Boot 2.x codebase with custom TagContributor adding 'custom.method' tag to metrics
examples.output: ExtendedServerRequestObservationConvention class that overrides getLowCardinalityKeyValues() to append KeyValue.of("custom.method", context.getCarrier().getMethod())
examples.notes: Preserves all default observation tags while injecting custom dimension

examples.input: Need to add application-specific request context (e.g., tenant ID) to observations
examples.output: Custom convention extracting tenant ID from ServerRequestObservationContext and returning KeyValue.of("tenant.id", tenantId)
examples.notes: Ensure tenant ID is bounded cardinality to avoid metric explosion

metadata.prompt: Create a custom class extending DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention. Override getLowCardinalityKeyValues() to call super.getLowCardinalityKeyValues(context) and chain .and(custom(context)) to append your custom KeyValue. Define a protected custom() method that returns KeyValue.of("key", value) extracted from the ServerRequestObservationContext. This pattern preserves all default observation tags while injecting your custom metric dimensions.

skill_drafts.name: Custom ServerRequestObservationConvention Implementation
skill_drafts.description: Implement ServerRequestObservationConvention to define metric name, trace name, and low-cardinality KeyValues for HTTP server request observations in Spring Boot 3.0. Use when completely replacing deprecated instrumentation filters with custom observation logic.
applicable_signals: Observation support integrated into Spring Boot 3.0
Previous TagProvider, TagContributor, or Tags classes deprecated
contraindications: Only adding supplementary tags to default behavior (use DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention extension instead)
Observation instrumentation is disabled or not required
No custom naming or tagging logic needed
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Create a new class implementing ServerRequestObservationConvention interface'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Implement getName() method returning the metric name string'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Implement getContextualName(ServerRequestObservationContext context) method extracting request method and returning trace name'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Implement getLowCardinalityKeyValues(ServerRequestObservationContext context) method building and returning KeyValues from context'}
{'step': 5, 'action': 'Register the implementation as a Spring bean (via @Component, @Bean, or configuration)'}
{'step': 6, 'action': 'Verify observation is applied by checking metric exports and trace output'}
triggers: WebMvcMetricsFilter or MetricsRestTemplateCustomizer deprecated and removed
Full control over HTTP observation naming and tagging required
Custom metric or trace naming strategy needed
constraints: Must implement all three required methods: getName(), getContextualName(), getLowCardinalityKeyValues()
Context parameter provides access to ServerRequestObservationContext
KeyValues must be low-cardinality to avoid metric explosion
Bean must be registered in Spring context for automatic application
cautions: High-cardinality KeyValues (e.g., user IDs, request IDs) can cause memory and performance issues; use only low-cardinality dimensions
Ensure metric and trace names are stable and do not vary per request
Test observation output to verify metric names and tags are generated correctly
output_contract: ServerRequestObservationConvention bean is registered and active; HTTP server requests generate observations with metric name, trace name, and KeyValues as defined by the convention; observations are exported to configured metrics and tracing backends

examples.input: HTTP GET request to /api/users with Spring Boot 3.0 observation support enabled
examples.output: Metric name: 'http.server.requests'; Trace name: 'http get'; KeyValues include method=GET, status=200, exception=none
examples.notes: Custom convention fully replaces deprecated WebMvcMetricsFilter behavior

examples.input: Extending DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention to add custom KeyValue
examples.output: Default KeyValues preserved plus custom KeyValue (e.g., custom.method=GET) appended
examples.notes: Use extension pattern when only supplementary tags are needed, not full convention replacement

metadata.prompt:
Create a class implementing ServerRequestObservationConvention with three required methods:
1. getName() - returns the metric name (e.g., "http.server.requests")
2. getContextualName(ServerRequestObservationContext context) - returns the trace name based on request context
3. getLowCardinalityKeyValues(ServerRequestObservationContext context) - returns KeyValues for observation tagging

Extract values from context.getCarrier() (the HTTP request) and build KeyValues using KeyValues.of() or KeyValue.of().

skill_drafts.name: Spring Boot 2.x to 3.0 Instrumentation Migration Reference
skill_drafts.description: Reference guide documenting deprecated instrumentation classes and their Spring Boot 3.0 replacements. Maps WebMvcMetricsFilter, MetricsRestTemplateCustomizer, TagProvider, and TagContributor to ServerHttpObservationFilter, ObservationRestTemplateCustomizer, and the Observation API. Explains why filters were removed (duplicate instrumentation risk, unresolvable bugs) and provides migration patterns.
applicable_signals: Assessing Spring Boot 2.x instrumentation code for 3.0 compatibility
Identifying deprecated instrumentation classes in existing codebase
contraindications: Do not use when implementing new instrumentation from scratch in Spring Boot 3.0 (use Observation API directly)
Do not use for applications already running on Spring Boot 3.0 without legacy instrumentation
Do not use as a step-by-step implementation guide; this is reference material only
triggers: assessing Spring Boot 2.x instrumentation code for 3.0 compatibility; identifying which classes and patterns must be refactored
constraints: Applies only to Spring Boot 2.x → 3.0 migration scenarios
Assumes familiarity with Spring Boot metrics and instrumentation concepts
Requires understanding of Observation API as the replacement framework
output_contract: Caller receives a clear mapping of deprecated classes to replacements (WebMvcMetricsFilter → ServerHttpObservationFilter, MetricsRestTemplateCustomizer → ObservationRestTemplateCustomizer), understanding of removal rationale, and code patterns for extending DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention or implementing ServerRequestObservationConvention.

metadata.prompt: Use this reference when assessing Spring Boot 2.x instrumentation code for 3.0 compatibility. Identify deprecated classes in your codebase and map them to their replacements. For TagProvider or TagContributor extensions, migrate to DefaultServerRequestObservationConvention or implement ServerRequestObservationConvention directly. Understand that filters were removed entirely due to duplicate instrumentation risk and unresolvable bug classes.
